name: Sable-Arc Concord Overcoat
description:
A long double-breasted overcoat in a heavyweight wool-cashmere blend, cut to fall just below the knee. Notched lapels wide enough to suggest authority without performing it. Six large buttons in a dark horn-composite. Fully lined in silk-weight acetate. The shoulders are structured without being padded — the coat holds its shape whether on a body or on a hanger. Available in charcoal, camel, and a deep midnight navy. Sable-Arc is a Tier 4 label with a flagship on the upper transit corridor, known for making exactly the kind of clothes that corporate directors wear when they want to look like they don't need to try.

This is a coat that says the meeting is already decided before you walk in. It's worn in boardrooms, in the climate-controlled corridors of Spire-adjacent towers, and occasionally by Tier 3 professionals who saved for three months to own one. It has no tech features. It doesn't need any. The fabric and the cut are the technology.
what_it_says: Power that doesn't announce itself. You've been in enough rooms to know that the coat does the work before you speak.
worn_by: Tier 3 aspirational buyers who saved for it
story_hooks: Sable-Arc's head of design has been quietly embedding a single thread of a proprietary dye in each coat's lining — invisible to the naked eye, readable under specific UV frequencies. The company claims it's anti-counterfeit. It is also a tracking marker.

A Tier 3 paralegal who scrimped to buy a secondhand Concord overcoat has been using it to move through Tier 4 spaces unchallenged — until someone who actually knows the label noticed the coat was two seasons old and started asking questions.

Three Concord overcoats were found in an abandoned Tier 2 storage unit, unworn, tags still attached, belonging to a corporate executive who disappeared eight months ago and was never reported missing.

physical_description.visual_profile: A commanding silhouette that drapes with understated authority. The overcoat falls just below the knee with a clean, unbroken line from shoulder to hem. Wide notched lapels frame the chest without aggression. The structured shoulders create a subtle power line across the body. Overall impression: someone who enters a room and the conversation shifts.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not tight—cut to accommodate layers beneath without clinging. The chest has subtle ease for movement; the waist suggestion is implied rather than cinched. The sleeves are long enough to hide wrist augmentation ports if desired. Sits on the body like it was made for this specific person, even though thousands wear the same cut.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight wool-cashmere blend—approximately 85% wool, 15% cashmere. The blend gives it both structure and a subtle hand-feel that signals quality on first touch.
physical_description.texture: The exterior has a refined, dense nap with no visible pilling or breakdown. The weave is tight and clean, suggesting durability beneath luxury. Interior fully lined in silk-weight acetate, creating a frictionless glide when putting on or removing. Buttons are dark horn-composite—slightly warm to the touch, never cold like synthetics.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey (most common—reads corporate-neutral), with secondary options in camel (warming, less aggressive) or deep midnight navy (slight formality uptick). No pattern, no accent colors. Purity through restraint.
physical_description.closures: Six large dark horn-composite buttons, double-breasted configuration. Button placement is deliberate—allows for partial closure in a relaxed stance or full formal arrangement. No magnetic snaps, no friction-fit; the coat relies on traditional button engineering.
distinctive_features: Notched lapels wide enough to convey authority without visual aggression
Fully functional but invisible hand pockets—deep enough for personal devices or a neural interface module
Internal breast pocket reinforced for credential holders or encoded identity chips
Horn-composite buttons age subtly with wear, developing character patina over years
Hem weighted with a thin acetate ribbon to prevent flutter and maintain line integrity
Seams are flat-felled and hand-finished on Tier 1 variants; machine-executed on Tier 4 versions but still immaculate
No visible branding on exterior—Sable-Arc's mark is inside the collar only, woven into the silk lining
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 aspirational—accessible to senior working-class professionals and lower-tier corpo staff. Worn by people who've earned enough to signal taste without displaying wealth ostentatiously.
physical_description.cultural_context: Corporate directorate, institutional authority, professional restraint. Worn by: mid-level executives in climate-controlled tower corridors, institutional administrators, financial advisors, medical procurement officers. Signals: I have made decisions that affect others. I do not need to justify my presence.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in. New coats have a subtle sheen that dulls slightly after three months of wear. After a year, the fabric develops character—button areas show light patina, lapels soften, the interior lining shows the micro-creases of a body it knows well. Rarely patched or weathered; owners maintain these for a decade or longer.
